use_when:
Use a card to display content and actions on a single topic.
Cards should be easy to scan for relevant and actionable information.
Cards can serve as entry points into deeper levels of detail or navigation, such as a music album or details on an upcoming vacation.
Cards can be displayed together in a grid, vertical list, or carousel.
Use cards to contain related elements
Contents can include anything from images to headlines, supporting text, buttons, and lists
Can also contain other components in slot area.
Cards have flexible layouts and dimensions based on their contents. Configuration is done at subcomponent level: CardLayout.

dont_use_when.text: Don’t scroll within a card to reveal information
Cards shouldn’t contain content that can be swiped, such as an image carousel or pagination. Also, swipe gestures shouldn’t cause portions of cards to detach upon swiping.
Don’t let cards bump other elements out of the way. When a card is picked up, it appears in front of all elements, except app bars and navigation.
On a mobile device, cards can't internally scroll, as it could cause two scroll bars to be displayed.

best_practice: Adjust the card layout so content remains the main focus on large screens
When designing for large screens, use multiple columns to display content
Certain devices or user contexts require different components to meet platform expectations
Expand a card to reveal information
A card should only have one swipe action assigned to it
When moving a card, increase its elevation
On a mobile device, cards can expand to reveal more content, scrolling within the screen. Content within cards doesn’t scroll.

state.enable: `enable` is the resting card, flat on its surface with no elevation.

layout.orientation.vertical: `vertical` stacks the image above the text; use it where cards sit side by side, in a grid or carousel.
layout.orientation.horizontal: `horizontal` places the image beside the text, sharing the width evenly; use it in a vertical list where height is limited.

image.ratio.4:3: `4:3` is the default landscape crop, for photos of places and scenes.
image.ratio.1:1: `1:1` crops the image square, for dense grids or a single object as the subject.

image.state.idle: Pins the overlay: `hover` forces it on, `idle` forces it off.
image.state.hover: Pins the overlay: `hover` forces it on, `idle` forces it off.

placement.text: In a three-column grid of search results: three vertical cards side by side, one per stay
In a vertical list: two horizontal cards stacked in a column, each with an outlined "Book" Button in its slot

a11y.text: Renders its root as an <article> element
The favourite button is a native <button>
The favourite button carries `aria-pressed`, "true" by default
The favourite button's `aria-label` is `favoriteLabel`, which defaults to "Save to favourites"
The favourite button has tabIndex 0, so it is in the tab order
Uncontrolled, clicking the favourite button toggles `aria-pressed`
Controlled through `favorited`, `aria-pressed` does not change on click until the owner updates it
The heart glyph is filled only while the favourite button is pressed
`overlayAction=false` removes the favourite button from the DOM
`:focus-visible` on the favourite button draws an outline of `--border-width-focused` in `--color-border-focused`, offset by `--border-width-default`
A supplied photo renders as with `alt` taken from `imageAlt`
With no photo supplied, an empty <div> renders in its place

The title renders as a

element, not a heading element
The card's shadow transition is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
The image overlay's opacity transition is removed under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
